migration_findings.documented_constraint: Stopped instances cannot change GPU type. Existing data remains bound to provider/region; delete destroys it. Keep existing host and backups intact while a new target is independently validated.
state_preservation_plan: Do not stop/restart the active teacher or edit the current stop.
Use a separately named stoppable instance only after root resolves its exact budget, runtime cutoff, provider configuration and quota. Do not delete the current host to switch GPU type.
Stage public pinned model/runtime artifacts on the new target first. Revalidate actual driver, Docker, storage, image source/package hashes, GPU capability and generated tiny/NF4 save/reload tests.
Transfer only the role-restricted private training inputs and append-only records needed by the chosen experiment via protected SSH. Verify hashes and retain original state and backups.

Transfer final adapters/receipts back through protected channels; a new training node does not automatically replace the public API, data volume or ingress. A serving cutover needs independent contract/quality/latency/readiness proof.

cold_transfer_bytes_planning.note: Image layers can share/compress; this sum is a storage planning figure, not transfer benchmark. New-target network staging/restore time unmeasured.

compatibility_findings.second_a100_instance: Same SM80 shape minimizes GPU architecture changes and can separate teacher from candidate training. It does not share memory across machines or create a distributed trainer.
compatibility_findings.dual_a100_node: Current trainer maps the whole NF4 model to device0 and has no DDP/world-size setup. Two80GB cards are not one160GB device; DDP replicates weights and does not fix per-rank memory. FSDP/tensor/pipeline sharding requires actual code/checkpoint/gradient/accounting proof and topology checks.
compatibility_findings.h100: 80GB per GPU provides newer compute but not extra VRAM over current80GB. Any speedup is unmeasured. HopperSM90 requires re-bound compute-capability guards and actual kernels/driver validation.
compatibility_findings.h200: 141GB on a singleGPU directly increases per-device memory, avoiding a distributed rewrite; it is the preferred memory-upgrade candidate if budget and capacity permit. Speedup remains unmeasured.
compatibility_findings.candidate_kernel_state: Current image has no FLA/causalconv packages. Official FLA0.5.2 and fla-core0.5.2 wheels were only staged/hash-checked locally; no install. New kernel path needs numerical/gradient/parameter and performance proof. Causal-conv1d1.7.0PyPI provides only source.
